name: EP-15 Complaints and Maintenance Requests (Backlog)
w: Residents report problems in their room (a fan not working, a leaking tap, no hot water) and owners or staff report problems they find themselves. Each complaint is tracked from report to fix and routed to someone who can fix it: the hostel's own electrician, plumber or handyman when it has one, otherwise an outside worker from the hostel's list of trusted vendors. Today none of this exists: residents have no way into the app and owners track repairs by phone and memory. A fixed, fast repair is one of the main reasons residents stay, so this also reduces move-outs.
ac: E15-T1 Complaint records, categories and lifecycle
E15-T2 Owners and staff raise and manage complaints
E15-T3 Residents raise complaints from their room without an account
E15-T4 Residents track progress and confirm the fix
E15-T5 Photo and video attachments
E15-T6 Worker directory: on-site staff and outside vendors
E15-T7 Automatic routing to the right worker

out: Messages to residents and workers use the channels built in EP-11 (SMS, WhatsApp, email); this epic decides what is sent and when. No payroll for workers (EP-12). No marketplace payments to workers in this epic; E15-T13 only decides whether to build one.
dod: Not started. Each task has its own acceptance criteria. A resident can only ever see their own complaints, an outside worker only the one job they were sent, and both are proven by tests.

name: Complaint records, categories and lifecycle
w: Every later feature hangs off one well-defined complaint record. Its status must change only along allowed paths and every change must be on record, as allocations already are.
ac: complaints: hostel, room and optional bed, raised by (resident, owner or staff), category, priority, title, description, status, assigned worker, timestamps
Categories per hostel with sensible defaults: electrical, plumbing, carpentry, cleaning, internet, appliance, pest control, security, other; each mapped to a trade for routing
Statuses open, assigned, in_progress, on_hold, resolved, closed and reopened, with allowed transitions enforced by a database trigger
Every change (status, assignment, comment) is an immutable complaint_events row with actor and time
Hostel-scoped RLS like every other table; a complaint about a bed can mark that bed 'maintenance' in one step

name: Owners and staff raise and manage complaints
w: Owners and wardens spot problems on rounds and also take complaints in person or by phone. They need one place to log, assign and follow up every complaint.
ac: Owners and staff raise a complaint for any room or common area, optionally on behalf of a resident
A complaints list with filters (status, category, priority, room, worker, age) and server-side pagination, linked from the navigation and the dashboard work queue
A complaint page shows the history, comments, photos, worker and cost; staff can assign, comment, change status and close
The room page and resident profile list their open complaints

name: Residents raise complaints from their room without an account
w: Residents have no login today, and asking every resident to create an account would stop most of them from reporting anything. A QR code in each room opens a short form; the resident proves who they are with the phone number already on their record.
ac: Each room has a printable QR code (from the room page) linking to a public complaint form for that room, using an unguessable per-room token that the owner can regenerate
The resident enters the mobile number on their record and confirms a one-time code by SMS; only residents with a live allocation in that room are accepted
The form has category, description and optional photos, and is usable on a cheap phone
Rate limits per phone and per room stop spam; a wrong or unknown number gets the same neutral message as a correct one
Owners can turn resident complaints off for a hostel
SMS goes through an Indian provider with DLT-registered templates (shared with EP-11)
out: No resident app or full resident portal; a resident session lasts only long enough to raise and follow complaints.

name: Residents track progress and confirm the fix
w: A complaint that disappears into silence is worse than none. Residents should see that it is being handled, and only they can say whether it is really fixed.
ac: After raising, the resident gets a link (by SMS) to a status page for their own complaints only
They are told when a worker is assigned, when work starts and when it is marked resolved
The resident confirms the fix or reopens it with a reason; complaints not answered in a set number of days close automatically
An optional 1 to 5 rating and comment on the fix, shown to the owner

name: Photo and video attachments
w: A photo of the leak tells the plumber what to bring. Attachments hold images of residents' rooms, so they must be private.
ac: Up to 5 photos or 1 short video per complaint, and completion photos from the worker
Stored in a private bucket under <hostel>/<complaint>/, checked by real file type and size like ID proofs, served through short-lived signed URLs
Images are resized on upload to keep storage and mobile data small
Only members of the hostel, the resident who raised it and the assigned worker's job link can open them

name: Worker directory: on-site staff and outside vendors
w: Routing needs to know who can fix what. Some hostels employ an electrician or caretaker; most call the same local plumber every time.
ac: Owners record workers per hostel: on-site (linked to a staff account or just a name and phone) or outside vendor (name, business, phone, trades, call-out charge, notes)
Each worker has one or more trades (electrician, plumber, carpenter, cleaner, technician, pest control, general)
A worker can be marked unavailable (leave, busy) for a date range
Vendors can be shared across an owner's hostels

name: Automatic routing to the right worker
w: The point of the feature is that nobody has to decide who to call every time. A complaint should reach the right person on its own, preferring the hostel's own staff.
ac: A new complaint is routed by its category's trade: first an available on-site worker with that trade, then the hostel's preferred vendor for the trade, then any vendor with the trade
With several matches, the one with the fewest open jobs gets it
When nobody matches, the complaint stays open and the owner is told it needs a worker
Owners can turn auto-routing off per category and assign or reassign by hand at any time; every assignment is logged
Routing runs in the database so two complaints at once never double-book by mistake

name: Job link for outside workers, no account needed
w: Outside electricians and plumbers will not install an app or create an account. They should get a message with a link that shows the job and lets them update it.
ac: An assigned outside worker gets an SMS or WhatsApp message with a link to that one job: hostel address, room, category, description and photos
The link uses an unguessable token, works only for that job, and expires when the job is closed or reassigned
From the link the worker accepts or declines, marks 'on the way', 'started' and 'done' with a note and completion photos, and enters the charge
A decline sends the job back to routing; no answer within a set time alerts the owner
The resident's phone number is not shown to the worker unless the owner allows it; on-site staff use the normal app instead

name: Repair costs and who pays
w: Every repair costs something, and owners need to know whether the hostel absorbs it or the resident pays (for example damage they caused).
ac: Each complaint records labour and material costs and the vendor's charge
The owner marks who pays: the hostel, or the resident; a resident charge becomes an ad-hoc charge on their next invoice (EP-13, E13-T2)
Payments made to outside vendors are recorded with mode and reference (a payout log, not a payment gateway)
Monthly maintenance spend per hostel and per category

name: Response targets, reminders and escalation
w: A complaint that sits for days is how residents lose trust. Each priority gets a target, and missed targets are flagged before residents have to chase.
ac: Per hostel, a response and a resolution target per priority (for example urgent: respond in 2 hours, fix in 24)
Complaints approaching or past their target are highlighted in the list and on the dashboard
Missed targets notify the assigned worker, then the owner
Targets pause while a complaint is on hold, with a reason

name: Complaint reports and recurring problems
w: Owners decide what to replace from patterns: the same geyser failing every month, one floor's wiring, a vendor who is always late.
ac: Complaints per category, room and floor over a period, with average response and resolution times
Rooms with repeat complaints in the same category are flagged
Vendor and staff performance: jobs done, average time, resident ratings, declines
Exports to CSV, computed in the database without the 1000-row API cap

name: Recurring preventive maintenance
w: Some work is predictable: water tank cleaning, pest control, fire extinguisher checks, AC servicing. Scheduling it stops it becoming a complaint.
ac: Owners define recurring tasks with a frequency, area and trade
Due tasks become complaints of type 'scheduled' and go through the same routing
Completed and overdue scheduled tasks are reported separately from resident complaints

name: Platform worker network (discovery)
w: Hostels without their own vendors would benefit from workers supplied by Hostel ERP itself. That is a different business (worker vetting, liability, payments, commission), so it is decided before anything is built.
ac: Write up the options: partner with an existing home-services provider through their API, build a vetted local network city by city, or stay with each hostel's own vendors
For each option: worker verification (ID and police verification), liability for damage or misconduct, pricing and commission, payment flow and GST
Decide with the owner; if a network is chosen, it becomes its own epic
Until then, the hostel's own vendor list (E15-T6) is the only source of outside workers
out: No building of a marketplace in this task.

name: Security tests for complaint access
w: This epic opens the app to two new kinds of user who are not members of the hostel: residents and outside workers. Each must reach exactly their own data.
ac: A resident can see and change only complaints they raised, and only while their phone verification is valid
A worker job link reaches only its one job; expired, reassigned and guessed tokens are refused
Members of other hostels cannot read complaints, attachments or workers, added to the cross-tenant RLS suite
Rate limits on OTP and complaint creation are covered by tests
